main.title: Stanford CS143: Compilers
main.why: Lexing, LL and LR parsing, semantic analysis and type checking, runtime organization, code generation, dataflow optimization, register allocation and garbage collection. In English.

main.title: The FORTRAN Automatic Coding System
main.why: Hand-coding dominated the cost of scientific computing, so FORTRAN compiled math-like programs and used flow analysis to assign registers about as well as people.

main.title: Efficiently Computing Static Single Assignment Form and the Control Dependence Graph
main.why: Optimizers kept tracing which assignment reaches each use, so SSA form gives every variable a single assignment and places merges at dominance frontiers.

main.title: LLVM: A Compilation Framework for Lifelong Program Analysis & Transformation
main.why: Compilers optimized once behind a private IR, so LLVM keeps a typed SSA representation that tools can optimize again at link time and run time.

further.title: BOLT: A Practical Binary Optimizer for Data Centers and Beyond

main.title: MLIR: A Compiler Infrastructure for the End of Moore's Law
main.why: Each domain-specific compiler rebuilt its own IR stack, so MLIR lets dialects at different levels of abstraction share one infrastructure and lower into each other.

main.title: Optimizing Dynamically-Typed Object-Oriented Languages With Polymorphic Inline Caches
main.why: Dynamic dispatch hides types from the compiler, so polymorphic inline caches record each call site's receiver types and hot code is recompiled for them.

main.title: Maglev - V8's Fastest Optimizing JIT
main.why: TurboFan arrives too late for code that is only warm, so V8 added Maglev, a quick optimizing tier built from bytecode and type feedback.

main.title: A Theory of Type Polymorphism in Programming
main.why: Untyped programs fail at run time and typed ones need annotations, so Milner's algorithm W infers polymorphic types, and well-typed programs cannot go wrong.

main.title: Gradual Typing for Functional Languages
main.why: Static and dynamic typing each suit different tasks, so gradual typing lets typed and untyped code mix, checking at run time where they meet.

main.title: Getting to Go: The Journey of Go's Garbage Collector
main.why: Go wanted short pauses without moving objects, so its collector went concurrent and dropped generational designs whose always-on write barrier cost too much.

further.title: Why Discord is switching from Go to Rust

main.why: FollowFeed's huge heap stalled G1 and non-generational ZGC, so LinkedIn flattened cached objects to cut headers and allocations, then moved to generational ZGC.

further.title: Bending pause times to your will with Generational ZGC

main.title: Safe Systems Programming in Rust
main.why: Systems code needs control without memory bugs, so Rust checks ownership and borrowing at compile time and confines unsafe code behind safe APIs.

further.title: Eliminating Memory Safety Vulnerabilities at the Source

main.title: Threads Cannot Be Implemented as a Library
main.why: Compilers can break correct threaded code when threads come from a library, so Boehm argues C and C++ must define a memory model.

further.title: Foundations of the C++ Concurrency Memory Model

main.title: Bringing the Web up to Speed with WebAssembly
main.why: JavaScript was a poor compilation target, so the browser vendors designed WebAssembly, a bytecode with formal semantics that validates fast and runs near native speed.
Prime Video's JavaScript app ran slowly on many TVs, so Amazon moved its low-level systems to Rust compiled to WebAssembly, beside the JavaScript VM.

main.title: Scaling Static Analyses at Facebook
main.why: To catch crashes and security bugs before code ships, Facebook runs compositional analyzers, Infer and Zoncolan, on every code change and comments during code review.

further.title: Lessons from Building Static Analysis Tools at Google

main.why: Go's nil checker found only obvious dereferences, so Uber's NilAway infers nilability across functions as constraints and reports contradictions on every build.
